title: Start Your Engines
summary:
Start Your Engines
This weekend may serve as one of the first official tests of whether demand for products can withstand current price levels. With crude oil prices hovering around $130 per barrel, refined product prices have been on the rise as well. The American Automobile Association estimates that 37.87 million Americans will travel 50 miles or more this weekend, marking a .9% decrease from last year.

children.title: Diesel does it
children.summary: Higher diesel prices in the States have directly contributed to gasoline stock draws in recent weeks: refiners are not replenishing gasoline stocks and concentrating on more profitable diesel production. The chart below shows the relative stock levels for both diesel and gasoline.

children.title: Gasoline Stocks
children.summary: Distillate Stocks The current supply balance for gasoline suggests that short-term demand bursts, such as the holiday weekend, can contribute to a price spike. In addition, diesel's favorable pricing reduces refiners' incentive to produce gasoline, thus supporting overall higher gasoline price levels in the longer-term.
